newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales up 0.6% in Jan.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales up 0.6% in Jan.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following seasonally adjusted data on UK retail sales in January.
RETAIL SALES VOLUME JAN DEC (DEC PREL)
Monthly s/adj change 0.6 -0.8 (-0.8)
Yr-on-yr change 4.6 3.0 (2.9)
Market forecasts had centred on a 0.3 percent rise in retail sales on the month and a year-on-year increase of 3.9 percent.
BY SECTOR (percentage gain, minus indicates fall)
m/m y/y 3m/3m 3m/3m yr ago
Predominantly food 0.5 3.8 1.3 3.2
total pred non-food 1.1 6.4 1.0 5.1
non-specialised -1.5 6.7 2.8 7.1
Textile,clothing,foot 1.4 5.8 1.2 5.6
Household goods 0.7 9.7 1.4 7.1
Other stores 2.5 3.7 -0.3 1.6
nonstore retail/repair -2.8 -3.2 -2.8 -0.8
The average weekly non-seasonally adjusted value of retail sales in January was 3,040 million stg, 7.1 percent up on January 1996.
In value terms, retail sales rose by 6.4 percent in the three months to the end of January on the same period a year earlier.

In the November to January period the value of sales, unadjusted, by predominantly food stores was 5.2 percent higher than a year earlier, the ONS said. Sales by predominantly non-food stores were up eight percent.
The near-record 4.6% year-on-year increase in sales -- the highest since March 1989 -- basically reflects the fact that the performance in January 1996 was poor, the ONS said.
Sales fell 1.0 percent on the month in January last year.
January 1997 was a four-week trading period. Last January measured a five-week period.

The measuring periods from November and December 1996 started six days later than in 1995. This had the effect of decreasing the unadjusted value of sales in December compared with a year earlier. The effect on January was more neutral.
Seasonally adjusted data have taken account of that effect.
The ONS said clothing sales have recovered well since December as have furniture sales. Cosmetics and chemists have improved sales since December and since January 1996.
But the ONS said the improvement in sales was a fairly general one, rather than confined to specific areas.
